abilities.description: Reads anchor dimming and drift patterns to predict which skybridge will unravel next.
abilities.name: Decay Mapping

abilities.description: Flies silk-and-bone wind-gliders across the gulfs between islands.
abilities.name: Glider Piloting

characters.arc: Wren begins as a cautious observer who trusts only her charts. She learns to listen to rival enclaves, breaks neutrality, and becomes a bridge between them who persuades with shared stories as well as evidence.
characters.description: A sixteen-year-old apprentice cartographer of Lantern Reach with ink-stained fingers, a patched teal coat and a satchel of rolled charts. Orphaned when a minor span faded in her childhood, she was raised by the Cartographers' Guild and learned to read the sky as a ledger of shifting islands. Her careful re-survey of the archipelago first revealed that the skybridge decay follows a pattern and is accelerating.
characters.external_conflict: The Ironroot Wardens dismiss her maps as a child's drawings, and the Storm Singers insist the decay is natural and must not be disturbed.
characters.flaw: She trusts data over people and assumes the truth will persuade on its own merits.
characters.goal: Carry her decay maps across the archipelago and persuade the enclaves to jointly re-weave the failing skybridges.
characters.internal_conflict: She is torn between the Guild's vow of neutrality that raised her and her growing need to take sides to save the realm.
characters.motivation: She lost her parents to a fading skybridge and refuses to let anyone else lose their home to the drift.
characters.name: Wren Alder

abilities.description: Knows the unwritten Lantern Accord customs and can invoke them to force a hearing.
abilities.name: Accord Law

characters.arc: Tobias begins by shielding the Guild with silence. Wren's courage shames him into publicly backing her and spending his hard-won credibility on the cause.
characters.description: A sixty-year-old Guildmaster of the Cartographers' Guild, lean and stooped, with silver spectacles and a voice worn soft from decades of arbitration. He signed the Lantern Accord's last renewal as a young clerk and has watched its spirit erode ever since.
characters.external_conflict: The Wardens pressure the Guild to withhold its survey data, while Wren pushes him to publish it.
characters.flaw: He mistakes caution for wisdom and delays until action is nearly too late.
characters.goal: Keep the Guild respected by every enclave while quietly getting Wren's findings to those who can act.
characters.internal_conflict: He knows the maps prove disaster is coming but fears that speaking out will destroy the Guild's standing.
characters.motivation: He wants to preserve the Guild's neutrality because he believes it is the only trust still shared between the enclaves.
characters.name: Tobias Marlowe

abilities.description: Shapes and tunes resonance-stone anchors that hold skybridges in place.
abilities.name: Anchor Forging

abilities.description: Rallies and directs the Warden smiths with unquestioned authority.
abilities.name: Commanding Presence

characters.arc: Garrick hardens against Wren and bars her passage. After an anchor in his own hold dims, he must choose between pride and survival, ending by opening the Wardens' craft to a shared weaving.
characters.description: A broad, weathered Warden-Chief of Ironroot Hold in his fifties, with bark-brown skin, hands scarred by anchor-forging and a cloak clasped with a resonance-stone chip. He enacted the Tribute Edict after watching his people's craft go unrewarded for generations.
characters.external_conflict: He faces Wren's campaign for open repair, the Wanderers' resentment of the tribute, and dissent among his own smiths.
characters.flaw: His pride keeps him from admitting that hoarding the craft is hastening the collapse he claims to prevent.
characters.goal: Keep control of anchor-repair knowledge and force the other enclaves to recognize Ironroot's worth through tribute.
characters.internal_conflict: He privately suspects Wren's maps are right but cannot concede without discrediting his own Edict.
characters.motivation: He believes the Wardens' guarded knowledge is the only thing keeping Ironroot Hold from being exploited by the other enclaves.
characters.name: Garrick Ironroot

abilities.description: Senses air currents that shift island positions and foresees drift.
abilities.name: Wind Reading

abilities.description: Knows the verses used to weave starlight into skybridge spans at night.
abilities.name: Starlight Songs

characters.arc: Isolde dismisses Wren as a meddler. After seeing the maps match the wind-readings of her own songs, she teaches the weaving verses across enclaves and redefines her faith as stewardship.
characters.description: A tall, serene Storm Singer elder of the Mistral Spires, with white-streaked hair braided with wind chimes and pale eyes that seem to follow unseen currents. She has sung the air-songs for sixty winters and taught that the bridges, like the winds, rise and fall.
characters.external_conflict: She is pressed by Wren and the Wanderers to share the starlight songs, while the Wardens demand she side with them.
characters.flaw: Her certainty in doctrine blinds her to evidence that contradicts it.
characters.goal: Preserve the Storm Singers' tradition of non-intervention and guide the islands through the cycle gracefully.
characters.internal_conflict: Her songs hold the very weaving verses needed for repair, and she doubts whether withholding them is faith or fear.
characters.motivation: She holds that the decay is a natural cycle and that meddling will bring a worse unraveling.
characters.name: Isolde Vane

abilities.description: Flies gliders through the aether-rich winds and knows hidden routes between islands.
abilities.name: Aerial Navigation

abilities.description: Reads people, bargains and slips past patrols and checkpoints.
abilities.name: Street Cunning

characters.arc: Kest begins as a cynical guide who helps Wren for profit. Through shared danger he becomes her loyal ally and persuades the Wanderers to join the alliance.
characters.description: A wiry nineteen-year-old glider courier and smuggler of the Hollow Drift, with a sun-bleached scarf, a crooked grin and a glider patched from salvaged silk. He lost his family home when the Hollow Span fell and now ferries goods and secrets between islands.
characters.external_conflict: The Wardens hunt his smuggling routes over unpaid tribute, and the Wanderers are split on whether to cooperate.
characters.flaw: He distrusts every authority so deeply that he sabotages offers of help.
characters.goal: Win real protection and repair for the Hollow Drift, using his smuggling routes as leverage.
characters.internal_conflict: He is tempted to let the old enclaves suffer the drift but cannot bear to watch ordinary islanders fall with them.
characters.motivation: He wants the enclaves that ignored the Hollow Span's fall to answer for it and to restore a home for his displaced people.
characters.name: Kest Harrow

relationships.description: Tobias Marlowe mentors Wren Alder as Guild apprentice, but his caution to stay neutral clashes with her urgency to publish the decay maps.
Garrick Ironroot dismisses Wren Alder's maps and bars her from the anchors, because acknowledging them would undermine his Tribute Edict.
Isolde Vane opposes Wren Alder's call for intervention, while the match between the maps and her wind-readings slowly unsettles her.
Kest Harrow guides Wren Alder across the gulfs by glider, first for payment and later out of loyal friendship.
Garrick Ironroot hunts Kest Harrow for smuggling past the tribute, which deepens Kest's hatred of the Wardens.
Garrick Ironroot pressures Tobias Marlowe to withhold the Guild's survey data, testing the Guild's neutrality.
